platform_ServoPowerStateController: make dut_off detection EC dependent Currently, this test asserts whether a DUT is off by pinging it and hoping for no response. This is noisy, but more importantly, it doesn't actually answer the question whether the DUT is off, but rather whether it responds to pings. This change replaces that logic by querying the powerstate on the EC instead, and considering _anything_ that is not S0 to be off. BUG=None TEST=manual testing on my desk with servo-v4 + nocturne servo-v4 + flapjack both trigger properly when off Change-Id: I7966e86b313ae5f7f9abae5cebf5a74069f504af Signed-off-by: Ruben Rodriguez Buchillon <coconutruben@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1601727 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org>

dev-lang/rust: use llvm-libunwind as the unwinder This uses the statically linked llvm-libunwind as Rust's unwinder instead of the dynamically linked one from gcc_s. This adds about 30k to the binary size but rust binaries will no longer depend on gcc_s. This change required an upstream patch to make it build with cross-compilation. The libunwind code was missing from from the llvm fork shipped with the rustc source tarball for unknown reasons. The ebuild sources the llvm fork directly from github and places the libunwind source in the correct spot. Because gcc_s isn't linked, a latent bug in mosys's link step was seen on armv7 builds. There was a missing compiler builtin that gcc_s provided that is no longer there. This was fixed in this CL by including the default libs via `-C default-linker-libraries`, which pulls in LLVM's compiler_rt. See crbug.com/868726 for more details about the issue. shill: connection: Remove Binder Connection::Binder was previously used as a way of informing dependents when a Connection goes down. However, there is currently no code in Shill that actually needs this. The only Binder client is VPNService, but this usage is unnecessary. The lifetime of a Connection is controlled by Device, which will call SetConnection(nullptr) when removing an existing Connection, so VPNService can cleanly keep track of Connection removals without the use of Connection::Binder. Functionality will be added to VirtualDevice to map virtual devices onto physical devices. Doing this in Device rather than Connection allows for VirtualDevices to map to a physical Device even when the Device is not yet up (e.g. arc_wlan0 should still map to wlan0 even when we have not yet connected to a WiFiService). This also allows us to expose Device dependency information to the D-Bus interface (e.g. if we have both a cellular dongle and l2tp VPN, there is currently no clean way to determine which PPPDevice maps to which usage from the D-Bus interface). shill: connection: Add oif rules for all interfaces Previously, a pair of iif rules were added for all physical interfaces. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. In this case, at connect() time, the socket is still implicitly bound to INADDR_ANY (for AF_INET sockets), and source address selection must occur. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type. net-print/ippusbxd: Adding exponential backoff for print read requests Initiating read requests uses an asynchronous callback system where requests are sent to the printer and then a callback will fire with the printer's response. If the printer currently has no data to service the read request then it responds with a 0-byte message. This system lead to ippusbxd spamming the printer continuously with read requests that came back with empty responses. This change introduces exponential backoff so that if an empty response is received from the printer, ippusbxd will wait for increasingly long periods before issuing another request. This change significantly reduces syslog spam, and should result in faster communication with the printer.
